hbr2011.text: In an audit of 2,241 U.S. companies, only 37% answered a new web lead within an hour, and 23% never answered at all. Firms that responded within the hour were nearly 7 times as likely to reach a decision-maker as firms that waited longer.
hbr2011.source: Harvard Business Review, "The Short Life of Online Sales Leads", 2011

insidesales2013.text: When InsideSales audited real response times, nearly 1 in 4 companies believed they called new leads within five minutes. Only 5% actually did. The most common real number of follow-up attempts was zero.

drift2017.text: A test of 433 companies found only 7% responded within five minutes, and 55% hadn't responded after five business days.

locals2024.text: In a test of calls to local businesses, only 37.8% were answered by a person. 24.3% got no answer and no voicemail.

brightlocal2026a.text: 94% of consumers are open to leaving a review when a business asks. 74% only pay attention to reviews from the last three months.
brightlocal2026a.source: BrightLocal Local Consumer Review Survey, 2026 (1,002 U.S. adults)

brightlocal2026b.text: 47% of consumers won't use a business with fewer than 20 reviews, and 89% expect the owner to respond to reviews.
brightlocal2026b.source: BrightLocal Local Consumer Review Survey, 2026 (1,002 U.S. adults)

reichheld.text: Bain & Company's research on loyalty found that raising customer retention by 5% can raise profits by 25% to 95%.

callback.myth: If they're really interested, they'll call back.
callback.reality: Interest cools in hours, not days. The businesses that win are usually the ones that reply first and follow up on purpose.
callback.note: You may have seen "80% of sales happen after the fifth follow-up." That number is credited to an association nobody has been able to find. We don't use it.

marketing.myth: Marketing doesn't work in my industry.
marketing.reality: When ads "don't work", the cause is often what happens after the click: slow replies, no follow-up, no tracking. The ads get blamed for a system problem.

texts.flow: That's rare and valuable. Your business already runs without you at the center of every sale.
texts.*: This isn't a discipline problem. The business was built around you, so it waits for you. A clear process, a system that handles the repetitive first steps, and a team that runs it are what give that time back.

questions.sub: Google, Meta, Yelp, Angi, Thumbtack, and similar.

leaky.lead: You're paying to fill a bucket that has holes in it.
leaky.text: From your earlier answers, some of the inquiries those ads bring in wait too long or never get followed up. When that happens the ads usually get the blame, even though the gap is in what happens after the click.

fixFirst.text: Good timing. Fixing the system before buying traffic means every future ad dollar lands somewhere that can catch it.

solid.text: Your response and follow-up look solid, which means your ad spend has a real chance to pay off. Phase 2 looks at whether you can measure which ads bring customers, not just clicks.

ready.name: Ready to Scale
ready.line: Your basics work. The next gains come from measuring and automating what you already do well.

leaky.name: The Leaky Bucket
leaky.line: You pay to bring inquiries in, and some of them slip out before anyone follows up.

secret.name: The Best-Kept Secret
secret.line: Your customers are happy, but almost nobody else can see it.

bottleneck.name: The Owner Bottleneck
bottleneck.line: The business grows as far as your calendar allows, and not much further.

silent.name: The Silent Leak
silent.line: Inquiries arrive, but there's no reliable path from first contact to a closed sale.

access.title: New inquiries wait for whoever is free.
access.step: One front door: every call, text and form lands in one place, gets an instant reply, and can book a time on its own.

pipeline.title: Your pipeline lives in several places, and partly in your memory.
pipeline.step: One shared list of every open inquiry, with its stage and the next action. Nothing fancier than that to start.

followup.title: Quotes go quiet and nobody chases them on purpose.
followup.step: A simple follow-up sequence that runs for every quote that hasn't closed, so it doesn't depend on anyone remembering.

reputation.title: Happy customers aren't turning into visible proof.
reputation.step: An automatic review request after every completed job, sent to every customer while the experience is fresh.

owner.title: Sales depend on your personal availability.
owner.step: Write down who handles each first step, then let the system do the repetitive parts so the team can run them without you.

notYet.platform: An all-in-one platform with dozens of features. Start with one shared list and one front door.
notYet.adBudget: A bigger ad budget. First close the gaps that lose the inquiries you already pay for.
notYet.moreAds: More advertising. Fix the system first so paid inquiries don't leak.
notYet.customApp: A custom app, or anything that requires you to become technical.
